text:
maya: Quick heads-up — planning a terraform apply against release-merge (prod-us-west) at 08:00 UTC. Changes: add IAM role for model-serving, small provider bump in infra-modules. I want the deploybot to hold the apply until we confirm provider pin and smoke tests.

deploybot: preflight: running `terraform plan` on branch release-merge...

deploybot: plan summary: +3 resources, ~1 resource to update, 0 deletes. no drift detected. provider mismatch: module/networking currently uses hashicorp/aws 3.5.0, target bump to 3.6.0 requested by infra-mods.

sam: Can we avoid a full provider bump in this window? If provider change is required for a minor nicety, prefer pinning to 3.5.1 for safety. Also: need an explicit rollback step for the IAM role add (timed disable path).

alex: Agreed on pin. Add `version = ">= 3.5.1, < 3.6.0"` to the provider block in modules/networking and module/iam. That avoids transitive surprise.

juan: For rollout: do a canary shift first. 10% traffic to new role for 30m, run smoke: /health, /auth, token rotation test. If anything >5% error, bail to previous (100% fallback).

ops-oncall: Change window ok 08:00-09:00 UTC. Please add a runbook note and set alerting thresholds. If high error or deploybot reports failed apply, page oncall and put the release in hold. Also record release notes blurb about the IAM role.

maya: plan snippet:

```
# terraform plan (truncated)
+ aws_iam_role.redwood_model_serving
+ aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.model_attach
~ aws_instance.app (update)
```

maya: @deploybot please hold at queue entry. I will update provider pins and add rollback runbook by 07:45 UTC.

deploybot: Hold placed by @maya. Queue position: 2. Preflight checks passed except provider version pin missing. To continue: remove hold with `/deploybot resume 7470012345`.

sam: I drafted rollback steps in the release notes draft: disable new role (set `active=false` in IAM module), revert provider pin, reapply. Also added a quick tfstate snapshot step: `aws s3 cp s3://tfstate/releases/release-merge.tfstate ./snapshot-7470012345.tfstate` before apply.

alex: Pushed provider pin to `module/networking` and `module/iam` in branch `infra/pin-3-5-1`. Running `terraform fmt` and `pre-commit`. Will link PR in a minute.

maya: PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/912. Tagging @juan to confirm smoke tests and canary automation exists.

juan: Canary config exists. I'll attach the canary manifest to this thread and schedule 10% for 30m post-apply. Also added smoke script at `ops/smoketests/iam_smoke.sh`.

deploybot: Preflight re-run: provider pins found. plan unchanged. All preflight checks PASS. Queue position: 1. Ready to execute once hold removed.

maya: Removing hold at 07:55 UTC, will trigger at 08:00. Final checks: ops-oncall monitoring ready? @ops-oncall

ops-oncall: Monitoring configured: dashboards, alerting (>=5% 5m error), and SLO rollback trigger. Oncall standby 07:50-09:30 UTC. :thumbsup:

sam: LGTM. I'll watch for auth failures. If we hit threshold, we execute rollback steps and open a postmortem if >30m outage.

maya: Starting apply now (08:00 UTC). Running `/deploybot apply 7470012345 --auto-approve`.

deploybot: APPLY started. logs: https://deploys.internal/7470012345

deploybot: APPLY complete — 3 added, 1 changed, 0 destroyed. Smoke tests queued.

juan: Canary shift to 10% now. Running smoke `/ops/smoketests/iam_smoke.sh`.

juan: Smoke results: all tests passed (auth, token-rotation, ACL check). Observability: error rate steady.

ops-oncall: No alerts. Latency stable.

maya: Great. Rolling to 100% traffic over next 10m.

sam: Noted rollback command if needed:
`terraform state rm aws_iam_role.redwood_model_serving && terraform apply -target=module/iam --auto-approve`

maya: Closing thread and adding release note: "added redwood_model_serving IAM role for model-serving, provider pinned to 3.5.1 to avoid upgrade surprises. Rollback steps documented." Thanks everyone.

ops-oncall: :thumbsup:
